work_items.title: Development-only ISmsSender that logs the full customer OTP, gated by env + Sms:DevLogCode flag
rule_citations: CLAUDE.md → project-specific facts (FakeItEasy cannot proxy ILogger over internal T)
acceptance_criteria: In Development, POST auth/customer/request-code prints the full 6-digit code to the API console (via DevConsoleSmsSender logging the raw body at Information, with the phone MASKED to last-4); the code then works with POST auth/customer/verify-code to issue a customer JWT.

In a non-Development environment the code is NEVER logged — only the masked marker (last-4 phone) — even when Sms:DevLogCode=true; the IHostEnvironment.IsDevelopment() check is the sole guard (the flag never reaches the sender).

RequestCodeEndpoint is unchanged; the masked ConsoleSmsSender remains the default whenever Sms:DevLogCode is unset/false. Base appsettings.json is untouched (GetValue<bool> defaults to false when the key is absent).

The dev branch masks the phone (last-4, same helper behavior as the masked/non-dev branch); ONLY {Body} is raw in the dev branch. The full E.164 phone is never logged in either branch — the only PII exception is the OTP body, and only in Development.

The AuthFeatureConfiguration factory selection is proven by an automated DI test: build a ServiceCollection + in-memory IConfiguration, run AddFeatureDependencies with Sms:DevLogCode=true then false then unset, resolve ISmsSender, and assert the concrete type (DevConsoleSmsSender when true; ConsoleSmsSender when false or unset). AC#1's dev-selects-code-logging and AC#3's masked-default are no longer only manually verified.

AuthFeatureConfiguration.AddFeatureDependencies XML <summary> is updated: describes the Sms:DevLogCode gate (DevConsoleSmsSender when true, else ConsoleSmsSender), says the ISmsSender lifetime is singleton (not scoped), and drops the stale 'registered unconditionally' claim.
Unit tests cover the dev-logs-code branch, the non-dev-masks branch, AND the factory sender-selection; existing ConsoleSmsSender and RequestCode/auth tests stay green.
dotnet build -warnaserror is clean and dotnet test is green.
test_cases: SendAsync_DevelopmentEnvironment_LogsFullBodyMaskedPhone: construct DevConsoleSmsSender with a hand-written ILogger<DevConsoleSmsSender> spy and a stub IHostEnvironment whose EnvironmentName = Environments.Development; call SendAsync("+420777123456", "Your Taxi verification code: 123456", ct); assert the spy captured a LogLevel.Information entry whose state/args CONTAIN the full body substring ("123456") AND do NOT contain the full phone ("+420777123456") — the {Phone} arg is the last-4 masked value (F2).

SendAsync_ProductionEnvironment_MasksAndOmitsBody: same sender with a stub IHostEnvironment EnvironmentName = Environments.Production (do NOT set the Sms:DevLogCode flag — it never reaches the sender); call SendAsync with a message containing the code; assert the captured log is the masked marker (last-4 phone) and does NOT contain the code/body substring. This is the production-safety pin for AC#2.
SendAsync_ProductionEnvironment_ShortPhone_MasksToStars: optional edge — phone shorter than 4 chars logs the fixed "****" marker (mirror ConsoleSmsSender behavior).

AddFeatureDependencies_DevLogCodeTrue_ResolvesDevConsoleSmsSender: build a ServiceCollection, AddLogging() AND AddSingleton<IHostEnvironment>(devStub) (the DevConsoleSmsSender factory branch resolves IHostEnvironment — a bare ServiceCollection does NOT register it, so resolution throws without this), create an in-memory IConfiguration with Sms:DevLogCode=true, call AuthFeatureConfiguration.AddFeatureDependencies(services, configuration), BuildServiceProvider, GetRequiredService<ISmsSender>(), assert it Is DevConsoleSmsSender (F1).
AddFeatureDependencies_DevLogCodeFalse_ResolvesConsoleSmsSender: same setup with Sms:DevLogCode=false → resolved ISmsSender Is ConsoleSmsSender (F1).

AddFeatureDependencies_DevLogCodeUnset_ResolvesConsoleSmsSender: same setup with NO Sms:DevLogCode key present → GetValue<bool> defaults false → resolved ISmsSender Is ConsoleSmsSender (F1, pins the AC#3 default).
Regression: existing auth/RequestCode integration tests still pass (they register their own fake ISmsSender via the factory, so the gated registration change is inert for them).
work_items.notes: SINGLE work item; backend-only, no new endpoint (no OpenAPI allowlist change). Class: internal sealed DevConsoleSmsSender(ILogger<DevConsoleSmsSender> logger, IHostEnvironment env) : ISmsSender in namespace Taxi.Api.Infrastructure.Sms. Dev branch logs event-style template `logger.LogInformation("Dev SMS {Phone} {Body}", masked, message)` where {Phone} is the SAME last-4 MASKED value used by the non-dev branch (F2 fix — the full E.164 phone is PII and is never logged; only {Body} is raw); non-dev branch mirrors ConsoleSmsSender exactly (`logger.LogInformation("Sms sent {Phone}", masked)` with last-4 masking, body never logged). Compute the masked value once (mirror ConsoleSmsSender's last-4 helper / inline masking behavior, incl. the '****' fallback for phones < 4 chars) and use it in BOTH branches. Add XML /// <summary> on the class plus a BOLD comment stating it is Development-only, why it intentionally logs the OTP BODY (and ONLY the body — the phone stays masked), and that the runtime IHostEnvironment.IsDevelopment() check is the guarantee against a production leak — this is the documented exception to rules/logging.md#what-must-not-appear-in-logs. Registration in AuthFeatureConfiguration: prefer a factory overload — `services.AddSingleton<ISmsSender>(sp => configuration.GetValue<bool>("Sms:DevLogCode") ? new DevConsoleSmsSender(sp.GetRequiredService<ILogger<DevConsoleSmsSender>>(), sp.GetRequiredService<IHostEnvironment>()) : new ConsoleSmsSender(sp.GetRequiredService<ILogger<ConsoleSmsSender>>()))` — preserve singleton lifetime and the ISmsSender service type; mirrors the Seed:Enabled precedent (one path chosen, order-independent). F3 — UPDATE the AddFeatureDependencies XML /// <summary>: it currently claims ConsoleSmsSender is 'registered unconditionally' and mislabels the lifetime as 'scoped'. Rewrite it to describe the Sms:DevLogCode gate (DevConsoleSmsSender when true, else the masked ConsoleSmsSender), state the ISmsSender lifetime is SINGLETON, and DROP the 'registered unconditionally' phrase (rules/csharp-style.md#xml-documentation). appsettings.Development.json gains `"Sms": { "DevLogCode": true }`; base appsettings.json's existing `"Sms": { "ApiKey": "" }` stays UNTOUCHED. TESTING TRAP: FakeItEasy IS in the test csproj but CANNOT proxy ILogger<T> over an internal T (DevConsoleSmsSender is internal) — use a HAND-WRITTEN ILogger<DevConsoleSmsSender> spy that records (LogLevel, message-template, state KVP args); assert on LogLevel + a substring of the args, never the full rendered string. The dev test asserts the code IS present AND the full phone is NOT (F2). For the IHostEnvironment stub, copy the ProductionEnvironment stub in api/tests/Taxi.Api.Tests/Geo/FleetKeyProtectorTests.cs (~lines 194-208) and make a Development twin (EnvironmentName = Environments.Development). F1 — the three factory-selection DI tests live in the SAME new file (api/tests/Taxi.Api.Tests/Infra/DevConsoleSmsSenderTests.cs); they need no logger spy (they build a real ServiceCollection with logging + an in-memory ConfigurationBuilder AddInMemoryCollection({"Sms:DevLogCode":"true"|"false"|omitted}), call AuthFeatureConfiguration.AddFeatureDependencies(services, config), BuildServiceProvider, and assert GetRequiredService<ISmsSender>() Is DevConsoleSmsSender/ConsoleSmsSender). DI-RESOLUTION TRAP for the true case: the factory lambda for the DevConsoleSmsSender branch calls sp.GetRequiredService<IHostEnvironment>(), but a bare `new ServiceCollection()` does NOT register IHostEnvironment (it comes from the Host builder, not the DI container). So the true-case DI test MUST `services.AddSingleton<IHostEnvironment>(devStub)` (reuse the Development IHostEnvironment stub you build for the behavior tests) or GetRequiredService<ISmsSender>() throws InvalidOperationException 'No service for type IHostEnvironment' BEFORE the type assertion runs. The env VALUE does not affect the resolved type — but the env REGISTRATION is required for the true branch to resolve. The false/unset cases resolve ConsoleSmsSender, which only needs ILogger, so AddLogging alone suffices there. Test file at api/tests/Taxi.Api.Tests/Infra/DevConsoleSmsSenderTests.cs (Infra/ holds real infra test cases; Infrastructure/ is test helpers/fakes only). Docs: add one line to docs/API-KEYS.md §2 (SMS) scoped clearly to the OTP/customer-auth ISmsSender path (distinct from the GoSms/SmsBrana Notifications provider that §2 otherwise documents; note §9's 'base Sms: section not used' caveat now has this single exception): in Development, Sms:DevLogCode=true (already set in appsettings.Development.json) prints the customer OTP to the API console so you can complete /customer login; never enable it in production.
